new_scholarship.description: The International Industrial Talents Education Special Program (INTENSE Program) is a Ministry of Education initiative, run with the National Development Council, participating universities and partner companies to recruit international students into industry-linked degree programmes in key fields such as STEM, finance and semiconductors. Admitted students receive full tuition and credit waivers for up to two years, a one-way flight ticket to Taiwan, initial administrative expense support and a monthly living allowance of at least NT$10,000 paid by the partner company, plus paid internships, in exchange for an obligation to work in Taiwan after graduation. Applications are made to individual participating universities, which publish their own deadlines for each Spring and Fall intake, so there is no single programme-wide application date.

Apply through the participating university's own online portal, not through any central INTENSE site.

Applying to the wrong intake - Spring and Fall rounds are roughly six months apart and do not coincide.

Being outside the programme's nationality restriction when it is limited to specific Southeast Asian countries.
Falling outside the top 50% of the class or scoring below 80 on conduct.
Underestimating the employment obligation - it is attached to the stipend and is contractually enforceable.
Assuming the funding package is identical across universities: at least one caps tuition subsidy at NT$50,000 per semester.

new_scholarship.notes: Critical money nuance: NT$25,000 per month is the TOTAL award, not the amount in the student's pocket. Participating universities deduct tuition and credit fees from that total first and split only the remainder into a monthly stipend. Taipei Tech publishes the resulting figures as around NT$14,000 per month in years 1 to 3 and NT$12,000 per month in year 4. Applicants should not budget on NT$25,000 of disposable income. Duration also varies by university: the standard MOE terms are 2 years for a master's and 3 years for a doctorate with annual review, while Taipei Tech runs the award for up to 4 years and restricts it to newly admitted PhD students. The scheme is quota-limited at 100 places per academic year, and waitlisted candidates approved by MOE must repay any previously disbursed stipends. new_scholarship.description: The MOE Elite Scholarship Program was created by the Ministry of Education of the Republic of China (Taiwan) under its New Southbound Policy to encourage university lecturers from South and Southeast Asian and African countries to pursue graduate degrees in Taiwan, with priority given to doctoral study. Awardees receive a total monthly award of NT$25,000 for up to two years of a master's programme or three years of a doctorate, reviewed annually; participating universities deduct tuition and credit fees from that total and pay the remainder to the student as a monthly stipend, which at Taipei Tech works out at around NT$14,000 per month in years one to three and NT$12,000 in year four. Applicants must currently hold a lecturer or more senior post at a university in an eligible country with that position on hold, must supply an up-to-date English Lecturer Certificate, and apply through the participating university, which submits the case for MOE review. Around 100 places are awarded per academic year across a three-year cycle.
